options.reason: An annual fatality count directly compares the number of motorist deaths recorded in each year.
options.answer: The data cannot establish whether risk per mile fell; annual motorist deaths were lower in 2025 than in 2013, falling from 110 to 81.
options.interpretation: This answers the question only as a comparison of the annual number of motorist deaths: the chart falls from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, with substantial fluctuation in between. It is a direct fatality-burden count, but it leaves unanswered whether an individual's risk per mile changed because the file has no miles-driven denominator.

options.denominator: All police-reported crash records in the same year
options.reason: Normalizing motorist deaths by reported crashes provides an available exposure-like comparison when miles traveled are not recorded.
options.answer: The data cannot establish per-mile risk; motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes increased from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025, so this crash-based proxy did not fall.
options.interpretation: This addresses whether fatalities declined relative to recorded crash volume: deaths per 100,000 police-reported crash records rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025. It is a defensible normalized proxy using an available denominator, but it does not measure risk per mile because the crash data contain no miles-driven measure.
